title: Quality and readiness
subtitle: Reaching a conclusion
objectives: Decide whether a wine is ready to drink

steps.title: BLIC
steps.body: Quality can be judged with four criteria, often remembered as BLIC: balance, length, intensity and complexity. A wine with all four is outstanding; with three, very good; two, good; one, acceptable. Faulty wines are poor. This avoids judging by personal taste alone.

steps.title: Readiness
steps.body: Readiness asks whether the wine will improve. A wine with high concentration, firm tannin or acidity and youthful aromas may gain complexity with time. A wine already fully developed, or light and fruity, should be drunk now. Wines past their best are too old. Grape, region and vintage help you decide.

steps.prompt: Match each BLIC criterion to what it asks.
steps.explanation: Together they judge quality without relying on personal taste.

steps.title: Writing the conclusion
steps.body: A full conclusion states quality and readiness, with reasons. For example: Very good. Balanced, with high acidity matched by intense fruit, a long finish, but limited complexity. Can drink now, but has potential for ageing. Reasons make your conclusion useful to others and to your future self.

steps.prompt: Which features suggest a wine has potential for ageing?
steps.explanation: Fully developed aromas suggest the wine is already at its peak.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Judge quality by balance, length, intensity and complexity
Concentration plus structure suggests ageing potential
